definition_zh: 与…一起；用；带着；随着；对…（表示态度）；由于
definition_en: a very common preposition meaning together with, by means of, having, or in relation to
core_image: 两个人的手同时落在一根扁担上，从两头一起把重物抬起来
scene: 两人把扁担搭上肩，一前一后同时起步，步子慢慢就合上了。 He came to the meeting with his father and a folder of papers.
sceneCN: 这里 with 是「与…一起」（第 1 个义项：表示伴随、同在）；句意为他带着父亲和一只文件夹来开会。两个人同时握住扁担抬起重物的那一刻，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 与…一起；用；带着；随着；对…；由于

senses.title: In company of
senses.definition: in the company of a person or an object, or carrying something
senses.definitionCN: 与某人或某物同在，或随身带着某物
senses.example: He came to the meeting with his father and a folder of papers.
senses.exampleCN: 他带着父亲和一只文件夹来开会。
senses.why: The oldest use simply puts two things in one place, side by side at the same moment.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法只是把两样东西放在同一处、同一时刻并列。

senses.title: By means of a tool
senses.definition: showing the tool, material or method that does a job
senses.definitionCN: 表示完成某事的工具、材料或方法
senses.example: She cut the bread with a long knife.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一把长刀切面包。
senses.why: The thing in your hand is the closest companion of the act, so company became instrument.
senses.whyCN: 手里握着的东西是动作最近的同伴，于是同伴变成了工具。

senses.title: Attitude towards someone
senses.definition: showing how a person feels about someone, as in angry with or pleased with
senses.definitionCN: 表示某人对某人的感受，如 angry with、pleased with
senses.example: The teacher was pleased with the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 老师对全班都很满意。
senses.why: Feelings are directed at people who are near, so the company sense turned into a sense of attitude.
senses.whyCN: 情感朝向近旁的人，于是相伴义变成了态度义。

senses.title: Changing together with
senses.definition: showing that two things change at the same time, as in with age or with time
senses.definitionCN: 表示两件事同时变化，如 with age、with time
senses.example: The colours of the leaves change with the season.
senses.exampleCN: 叶子的颜色随季节改变。
senses.why: Two events in step are also two things together, so the word covers parallel change.
senses.whyCN: 同步发生的两件事也是同在的两件事，于是这个词也覆盖并行变化。

intro.en: With is Old English wið, which first meant against, towards, or in exchange for, before it settled into together with.
intro.cn: with 是古英语 wið，最初意为对着、朝向或以物易物，后来才固定为「与…一起」。

items.en: A common Germanic preposition named the idea of being opposite or facing something.
items.cn: 一个共同的日耳曼语介词表示相对、面对某物的观念。

items.en: wið meant against, towards or in exchange for, and often marked opposition.
items.cn: wið 意为对着、朝向或以物换物，常标记对立。

items.en: The same word was used of a meeting between two parties, which carried the seed of togetherness.
items.cn: 同一个词也用于两方相遇，其中埋下了「同在」的种子。

items.en: The sense shifted from opposition to company, and wið became with.
items.cn: 词义从对立转向相伴，wið 变成 with。

items.en: The preposition widened to tools, possession, attitude and simultaneous change.
items.cn: 这个介词扩展到工具、拥有、态度与同步变化。

note.en: The first group collects prepositions built from the same stem, the second near synonyms of company and means.
note.cn: 第一组收由同一词干构成的介词，第二组收表示伴随与手段的近义词。

entries.definition: Inside a place or a period.
Not having, not accompanied by.
The power of clever thinking.
The measure from side to side.
Next to and together with.
Near, or by means of.
The negative of with.

normalIntro.en: With is a function word, so learn it as a set of frames rather than a single meaning.
normalIntro.cn: with 是功能词，把它当成一组句式框架来学，比记单一意思更有效。

normal.en: The th sound is soft and voiced, the same as in this and that.
normal.cn: 它的 th 是浊音，与 this、that 相同。

normal.en: With begins with wit minus the t: a preposition with no jokes inside.
normal.cn: with 就是 wit 去掉 t：一个没有玩笑的介词。

normal.en: Add out to make without, the opposite of company.
normal.cn: 加 out 得到 without，是相伴的反面。

normal.en: Add in to make within, the opposite of crossing a boundary.
normal.cn: 加 in 得到 within，是不越界的说法。

normal.en: With is often a tool, a companion, or a mood, so ask which of the three a sentence needs.
normal.cn: with 常表示工具、同伴或情绪，读到句子先问是哪一种。

abstract.en: Two hands on one pole, lifting at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 两只手在同一根扁担上，同时用力。

abstract.en: Two sets of footprints walking in the same line.
abstract.cn: 两串脚印走在同一条线上。

abstract.en: A hand holding a key that fits a lock.
abstract.cn: 一只手握着正好合锁的钥匙。

examples.en: I went to the market with my aunt.
examples.cn: 我和姑妈一起去了市场。

examples.en: He opened the box with a small screwdriver.
examples.cn: 他用一把小螺丝刀打开了盒子。

examples.en: The room grew quiet with the falling snow.
examples.cn: 随着雪落，房间安静下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: with 三张脸：一起、用、带着 —— 同伴、工具、随身的物。

root: 古英语 wið（对着、朝向、交换）→ 中古英语 with（与…一起）；同族有 within、without、withdraw。

sensesIntro.en: The preposition begins as opposition, turns into company, and spreads from people to tools, attitudes and simultaneous change.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个介词从对立开始，转为相伴，再从人扩展到工具、态度与同步变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands on one carrying pole, lifted at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手在同一根扁担上同时发力。

branches.en: The company branch: arriving with a father and papers.
branches.cn: 相伴分支：带着父亲和文件到场。

branches.en: The tool branch: bread cut by a long knife.
branches.cn: 工具分支：一把长刀切面包。

branches.en: The feeling branch: a teacher pleased with a class.
branches.cn: 情感分支：一个满意的老师。

branches.en: The change branch: leaves turning with the season.
branches.cn: 变化分支：随季节变色的叶子。

branches.en: The nearness branch: what is at hand becomes the means.
branches.cn: 邻近分支：手边之物成了手段。

intro.en: With is a bare preposition that joins other words as a prefix in within, without, withdraw and withhold.
intro.cn: with 是光秃的介词，作为前缀与其他词结合成 within、without、withdraw、withhold。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic, so the Latin entries are borrowed prepositions for the same ideas.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语，所以拉丁条目是表达同类观念的借入介词。

items.example: It appears in withdraw and withhold.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 withdraw 与 withhold 中。

definition_zh: 片刻；时刻；时机；重要性
definition_en: a very short period of time; a particular point in time; the right point for doing something; formal importance or weight
core_image: 秒针刚跳过去一格，屋里恰好安静下来
scene: 锅里水刚开，母亲转身去接电话，回来时饺子已经全浮了起来。 For a moment the kitchen was quiet enough to hear the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 moment 是「片刻、一会儿」（第 1 个义项：很短的一段时间）；句意为有短短一会儿，厨房安静得能听见雨声。画面里能想见：冒热气的锅、浮起的饺子、响起的电话。

collocations.zh: 关键时刻；见真章的一刻

derivatives.zh: 由 moment 加 -ary 构成，义为「瞬间的；短暂的」
由 momentary 加 -ly 构成，义为「片刻地；马上」
由 moment 加 -ous 构成，义为「重大的；影响深远的」
与 moment 同出拉丁语 momentum，义为「动量；势头」

senses.title: A very short period of time
senses.definition: a very short period of time, often shorter than a minute
senses.definitionCN: 很短的一段时间，常指不到一分钟
senses.example: For a moment the kitchen was quiet enough to hear the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 有短短一会儿，厨房安静得能听见雨声。
senses.why: Latin momentum first meant movement, and a moment is the smallest slice of movement you can notice, a tick of time that passes before anything else happens.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 momentum 起初表示「运动」，而 moment 就是你能察觉的最小一段运动：在别的事情发生之前先溜走的那一格时间。

senses.title: A particular point in time
senses.definition: a particular point in time, especially one that is remembered or waited for
senses.definitionCN: 某个特定的时间点，尤指被记住或等待的那一个
senses.example: The moment the lights went out, everyone froze.
senses.exampleCN: 灯灭的那一刻，所有人都僵住了。
senses.why: Once time is cut into ticks, one tick can be singled out and named; the word then stops being a length and becomes a marked position on the clock.
senses.whyCN: 时间一旦被切成格子，其中一格就能被单独挑出来命名；这个词于是不再表示长度，而表示钟面上的一个标记位置。

senses.title: The right point for doing something
senses.definition: the point at which something is best done, or when an important change becomes possible
senses.definitionCN: 最适合做某事的那个点，或重大变化可能发生的那个点
senses.example: The crisis became the moment for the old policy to end.
senses.exampleCN: 这场危机成了旧政策终止的时机。
senses.why: A single tick can carry a decision: when the word names one point, that point can also be the hinge on which later events turn.
senses.whyCN: 一格时间可以承载一个决定：当这个词指某一个点时，那个点也能成为后来事件转动所绕的轴。

senses.title: Importance or weight, in formal use
senses.definition: importance, especially in the phrase of great moment; a formal and rather old use
senses.definitionCN: 重要性，尤用于短语 of great moment；属正式而偏旧的用法
senses.example: The choice before the council was of great moment.
senses.exampleCN: 摆在议会面前的这个选择分量很重。
senses.why: Latin momentum also meant weight and influence, because something that moves carries force; English kept that sense for serious, formal matters.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 momentum 也指重量与影响力，因为运动的东西带着力量；英语把这个义项留给了严肃正式的场合。

intro.en: Moment is a contraction of a Latin word for movement, and its senses still follow the path from a moving body to a tick of time and to weight.
intro.cn: moment 是拉丁语表示「运动」的词缩合而来，它的义项仍沿着从运动之物到一格时间、再到分量的路线走。

items.en: Movere meant to move, and it supplied a large family of words about motion and change.
items.cn: movere 意为移动，派生出一整族与运动、变化有关的词。

items.en: Movimentum named a movement; in everyday speech the v dropped out and the word became momentum.
items.cn: movimentum 表示一次运动；在日常口语里 v 脱落，词形变成 momentum。

items.en: Momentum covered movement, the smallest division of time, and also weight or influence.
items.cn: momentum 兼指运动、最小的时间单位，以及重量或影响力。

items.en: Old French took the time sense as moment, meaning an instant, and passed it to English.
items.cn: 古法语取其中的时间义，写作 moment，意为瞬间，并传入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the short-time sense as the main one, adds the point-in-time and opportunity senses, and leaves importance to formal style.
items.cn: 现代英语以「短暂时间」为主体义项，又发展出时点与时机义，而「重要性」只留在正式文体里。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin movement root and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers words for instants, turning points and weight.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语「运动」词根及其英语词族展开；近义组收表示瞬间、转折点与分量的词。

entries.definition: Lasting only for an instant.
For a very short time, or very soon.
Of great importance, often because it changes a course of events.
entries.definitionCN: 重大的，常指会改变事态走向的。

entries.definition: The force of a moving body, or the push that keeps a process going.
entries.definitionCN: 运动物体的力；推动进程的势头。

entries.definition: An extremely short moment.
A very short space of time, used loosely.
entries.definitionCN: 宽松说法中的一小会儿；分钟。

entries.definition: A particular point in time, especially one where decisions must be made.
entries.definitionCN: 特定时刻，尤指必须作决定的关头。

entries.definition: The importance or meaning that something carries.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物所具有的重要性或意义。

normalIntro.en: The word is a shrunk Latin movement word, and every sense is a different reading of what that small movement marks: a tick, a point, a hinge, a weight.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「运动」一词的缩形，每个义项都是对那一小段运动所标记之物的不同解读：一格、一点、一轴、一份重量。

normal.en: Movere is Latin for to move; drop the v from movimentum and momentum appears.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语的「移动」；把 movimentum 里的 v 去掉，就得到 momentum。

normal.en: The -ment in movement and the -ment of moment come from the same Latin habit of building nouns out of verbs.
normal.cn: movement 的 -ment 与 moment 的 -ment 源自同一个用动词造名词的拉丁习惯。

normal.en: Momentary adds -ary: lasting only a moment.
normal.cn: momentary 加 -ary：只持续一个片刻的。

normal.en: Momentous adds -ous: full of moment, therefore heavy with importance.
normal.cn: momentous 加 -ous：满是分量，因而是重大的。

normal.en: At the moment points to now; in a moment points to just after now.
normal.cn: at the moment 指向现在；in a moment 指向现在之后的一小会儿。

abstract.en: A moment is what a moving world leaves behind when you stop the film for one frame.
abstract.cn: moment 就是你按下暂停键时，这个运动的世界留下的那一帧画面。

abstract.en: Anything that moves carries weight, which is why the same word can mean both an instant and a serious matter.
abstract.cn: 凡是运动的东西都带着分量，所以同一个词既能指一瞬，也能指严肃大事。

abstract.en: A hinge is a small point that decides which way a large door swings.
abstract.cn: 合页是一个小点，却决定一扇大门往哪边开。

examples.en: For a moment the kitchen was quiet enough to hear the rain.
examples.cn: 有短短一会儿，厨房安静得能听见雨声。

examples.en: The moment the lights went out, everyone froze.
examples.cn: 灯灭的那一刻，所有人都僵住了。

examples.en: The choice before the council was of great moment.
examples.cn: 摆在议会面前的这个选择分量很重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「默默」——沉默的一小会儿，就是片刻；moment 就是片刻、时刻。

root: 拉丁语 movere（移动）派生的 movimentum 缩合为 momentum（运动、瞬间、分量），经古法语 moment 进入英语；同族词多与运动、瞬间有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one tick of movement; the senses read that tick as a brief length, a marked point, a hinge for decisions and a measure of weight.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一格运动；义项把这一格读成一段短时长、一个标出的点、一处决策的轴心，以及一份分量的尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the second hand jumping one small step while the room falls silent.
core.cn: 核心意象：秒针刚跳过去一小格，屋里恰好安静下来。

branches.en: a kettle whistling, then silence for a breath
branches.cn: 水壶响过之后，静下一口气的工夫

branches.en: everyone looking up as the lights fail
branches.cn: 灯灭时所有人一起抬头

branches.en: a door left open at the exact second it matters
branches.cn: 在关键那一秒被推开的门

branches.en: a council raising a hand at the turning point
branches.cn: 转折点上举手的议事会

branches.en: a heavy file placed on a light table
branches.cn: 重文件压在轻桌子上

intro.en: A Latin verb of moving, its contracted noun, a French instant and four English endings turn a step of movement into time and importance.
intro.cn: 一个表示移动的拉丁动词、它缩合而成的名词、一个法语词和四个英语词尾，把一步运动变成了时间与分量。

latinIntro.en: Movere, movimentum and momentum are recorded Latin forms, and momentum is the direct source of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: movere、movimentum 与 momentum 都是有记录的拉丁词形，其中 momentum 是英语名词的直接来源。

belonging to, of the nature of
result or means of an action
items.meaningCN: 名词后缀：动作的结果或手段

definition_zh: 符号；迹象；招牌
definition_en: a mark with a meaning, a fact showing something, or a notice board
core_image: 门上一块木牌，白字写着方向
scene: 门上挂着一块牌子，上面写着「推」。 The sign on the door says Push.
sceneCN: 这里 sign 是「招牌、告示牌」（第 3 个义项）；句意：门上的牌子写着「推」。

senses.title: A mark with meaning
senses.definition: a mark or symbol that carries a meaning
senses.definitionCN: 带有含义的记号或符号
senses.example: The plus sign means add.
senses.exampleCN: 加号表示相加。
senses.why: This is the basic symbolic sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的符号义项。

senses.title: A fact showing something
senses.definition: something that shows a fact or a likely event
senses.definitionCN: 表明某个事实或可能发生之事的现象
senses.example: There is no sign of rain.
senses.exampleCN: 没有要下雨的迹象。
senses.why: Facts act like marks that point to more.
senses.whyCN: 事实就像指向更多信息的记号。

senses.title: A notice board
senses.definition: a board or notice that gives information or a warning
senses.definitionCN: 提供信息或警告的牌子
senses.example: The sign on the door says Push.
senses.exampleCN: 门上的牌子写着「推」。
senses.why: A board is a large public mark.
senses.whyCN: 牌子是一种大型的公共记号。

intro.en: Sign comes from the Latin word for a mark.
intro.cn: sign 来自拉丁语中表示记号的那个词。

items.en: Signum meant a mark or token.
items.cn: signum 意为记号或标志。

items.en: The word passed into French as signe.
items.cn: 这个词以 signe 的形式进入法语。

items.en: English borrowed it as signe.
items.cn: 英语借入时写作 signe。

items.en: The spelling became sign.
items.cn: 拼写变为 sign。

items.en: The verb use meant to write one's name.
items.cn: 动词用法表示写下自己的名字。

note.en: Sign is compared with similar-looking words and with words for marks.

abstract.en: A sign is a finger pointing at meaning.
abstract.cn: 记号是指向意义的一根手指。

abstract.en: Small marks carry large agreements.
abstract.cn: 小小的记号承载着重要的约定。

abstract.en: What we notice becomes a sign.

dict_mnemonic.text: sign 的核心是「记号」：小记号是符号，指向事实是迹象，挂在门上就是招牌。

root: 源自拉丁语 signum（记号、标志），核心义「有含义的记号」。

core.en: A visible mark that points to something else.
core.cn: 指向他物的可见记号。

branches.en: A plus sign stands for addition.

branches.en: Dark clouds are a sign of rain.

branches.en: A board tells people what to do.

intro.en: Sign builds a large family of marking and meaning words.
intro.cn: sign 构成一个表示标记与含义的大家族。

latinIntro.en: Sign comes through French from Latin signum, a mark.

definition_zh: 布；布料；一块布
definition_en: material made by weaving cotton, wool or other fibres
core_image: 一匹柔软的布，指尖一摸便起细纹
scene: 美术课上，同学们用一块布擦掉颜料。 Wipe the paint with a soft cloth, please.
sceneCN: 这里 cloth 是「一块布」（第 2 个义项：用来擦东西的那块布料）；句意是请用软布擦掉颜料。

derivatives.zh: 由 cloth  + suffix  -e 构成，义为「给…穿衣」
由 cloth 派生，义为「衣服」的总称
由 cloth 加 -ing 构成，义为「服装（总称）」

senses.title: Woven material
senses.definition: material made of woven fibres like cotton or wool
senses.definitionCN: 棉、毛等纤维织成的材料
senses.example: Mother bought two metres of cloth to make curtains.
senses.exampleCN: 妈妈买了两米布做窗帘。
senses.why: Weaving turns loose fibres into a flat sheet, and the flat sheet itself got the name.
senses.whyCN: 织造把松散纤维变成平整的一幅，这一整幅便得了名字。

senses.title: A piece of this material for cleaning
senses.definition: a single piece of cloth used to clean or cover things
senses.definitionCN: 用来擦东西或盖东西的一块布
senses.example: Hand me a damp cloth to wipe the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 递给我一块湿布擦桌子。
senses.why: A big sheet can be torn into small handy pieces for wiping, so a wipe-rag keeps the same name.
senses.whyCN: 大布可以撕成小块随手擦用，擦布便沿用同一名字。

senses.title: The textile trade or making
senses.definition: the making and selling of woven material
senses.definitionCN: 布料的织造与买卖
senses.example: The town lived on cloth for two hundred years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小城靠纺织活了二百年。
senses.why: When one material feeds a whole town, the material's name covers the trade too.
senses.whyCN: 当一种物料养活全城，它的名字也覆盖了这门行业。

intro.en: Cloth is one of the oldest words of everyday life, older than any written story about tailors.
intro.cn: cloth 是日常生活最古老的词之一，比任何关于裁缝的记载都古老。

items.en: The Germanic base *klotham is the starting point; its earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 起点是日耳曼语词基 *klotham，更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English clath meant a cloth or a garment.
items.cn: 古英语 clath 指布或衣物。

items.en: German Tuch and Dutch doek are cousins from the same old family.
items.cn: 德语 Tuch 与荷兰语 doek 是同一古老家族的亲戚。

items.en: Middle English cloth covered both the material and the made garment.
items.cn: 中古英语 cloth 既指材料也指做成的衣服。

items.en: Modern English split the work: cloth for material, clothes for worn things, clothing for the whole trade.
items.cn: 现代英语分工明确：cloth 指布料，clothes 指穿的衣服，clothing 指服装总称。

note.en: The first group collects the cloth family; the second collects fabric words.
note.cn: 第一组收 cloth 词族，第二组收面料类词。

entries.definition: Things you wear.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「衣服」，与 cloth 同源却只指成衣。

entries.definition: Garments in general.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「服装（总称）」，由 cloth 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: A maker or seller of clothes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「服装商；裁缝」，是 cloth 的老派生词。

entries.definition: Material made by weaving, often fine cloth.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「织物；面料」，与 cloth 同义而稍正式。

entries.definition: The stuff things are made from.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「材料」，范围更广。

entries.definition: Woven cloth, often in trade contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「纺织品」，多用于行业语境。

normalIntro.en: Remember cloth through its three relatives: clothe, clothes and clothing.
normalIntro.cn: 借三个亲戚 clothe、clothes、clothing 记忆 cloth。

normal.en: cloth is the material; clothes are what you wear.
normal.cn: cloth 是布料，clothes 是穿的衣服。

normal.en: the plural of cloth is cloths.
normal.cn: cloth 的复数是 cloths。

normal.en: a damp cloth wipes tables clean.
normal.cn: 湿布能把桌子擦干净。

normal.en: clothe the baby means put clothes on the baby.
normal.cn: clothe the baby 指给宝宝穿衣。

normal.en: cotton cloth feels soft in summer.
normal.cn: 棉布夏天摸起来柔软。

abstract.en: Feel the cool smooth slide of silk between your fingers.
abstract.cn: 感受丝缎在指间清凉顺滑地滑过。

abstract.en: Hear the soft swish of cloth folded on a table.
abstract.cn: 听布料在桌上被折起时的窸窣声。

abstract.en: See a bolt of blue cloth unrolled by a shopkeeper.
abstract.cn: 想象店主展开一匹蓝布。

examples.en: Cut the cloth along the red line.
examples.cn: 沿着红线裁布。

examples.en: She cleaned the blackboard with a dry cloth.
examples.cn: 她用干布擦了黑板。

examples.en: This town was famous for its fine cloth long ago.
examples.cn: 很久以前，这座小镇以精致的布料闻名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克罗斯」——布「洛」在手里软「丝丝」的，cloth 就是一匹柔软的布。

root: 日耳曼语 *klotham（来源不确定）→ 古英语 clath（布；衣物）→ 中古英语 cloth → 现代英语 cloth；同族词有德语 Tuch，派生词有 clothe（穿衣）、clothes（衣服）、clothing（服装总称）。

sensesIntro.en: Cloth stretches from a woven sheet to a wiping rag and a whole trade.
sensesIntro.cn: cloth 从织成的一幅布延伸到抹布和整个纺织业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat woven sheet, soft to the touch
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅摸上去柔软平整的织物

branches.en: The woven material itself
branches.cn: 织成的材料本身

branches.en: The wiping piece
branches.cn: 用来擦的那块

branches.en: The making and selling
branches.cn: 织造与买卖

branches.en: Cotton, wool and silk
branches.cn: 棉、毛与丝

branches.en: From fibre to garment
branches.cn: 从纤维到成衣

intro.en: Cloth fans out into the whole clothing family.
intro.cn: cloth 扩展出整个服装词族。

latinIntro.en: Cloth is Germanic, so its family is Germanic rather than Latin.
latinIntro.cn: cloth 属日耳曼词源，词族也是日耳曼而非拉丁的。

items.exampleCN: 他们给孩子们穿得暖暖的。

items.example: The clothier opened a new shop.

items.meaning: an old worn piece of cloth
items.example: He wiped the bike with a rag.

definition_zh: 名单；清单；列表；把……列成表
definition_en: a series of names or items written one below another; to write items in such a series
core_image: 一列竖着写下的名字，一条接一条
scene: 出门前，她在冰箱门上贴了一张纸条。 Check the packing list before you close the suitcase.
sceneCN: 这里 list 是「清单」（第 1 个义项：逐项写下的目录）；句意为合上行李箱前核对装箱清单。

derivatives.zh: list 加 -ing，指「列表；刊登信息」
与 list2（倾斜）相关，指「无精打采的」
list 与 agent 合成，指「（房产）挂牌经纪人」

senses.title: A series of written items
senses.definition: a set of names or items written one under another
senses.definitionCN: 逐项竖排写下的名字或条目
senses.example: Check the packing list before you close the suitcase.
senses.exampleCN: 合上行李箱前核对装箱清单。
senses.why: Items written one below another form the plain picture.
senses.whyCN: 逐项下写的东西构成最朴素的画面。

senses.title: To write items in a series
senses.definition: to write or put items into such a series
senses.definitionCN: 把条目写进或排入这样的系列
senses.example: The guide lists thirty waterfalls.
senses.exampleCN: 指南列出了三十处瀑布。
senses.why: The noun hardened into a verb: putting things into rows.
senses.whyCN: 名词固化为动词：把物排入行。

senses.title: An official register
senses.definition: an official published register of names or things
senses.definitionCN: 官方公布的名册或目录
senses.example: The waiting list doubles every winter.
senses.exampleCN: 候补名单每年冬天翻倍。
senses.why: Registers are just lists with authority attached.
senses.whyCN: 名录就是附上权威的清单。

senses.title: A border strip (old use)
senses.definition: a border or edge strip, as in the old phrase the list of the field
senses.definitionCN: 边界或镶边，如旧语 the list of the field
senses.example: Knights met within the lists.
senses.exampleCN: 骑士们在其界内比武。
senses.why: A border marked where the contest began and ended.
senses.whyCN: 边界标出比武的起止。

senses.title: To lean to one side
senses.definition: to lean over to one side, said of ships
senses.definitionCN: 指船身向一侧倾侧
senses.example: The old ferry listed after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 渡轮在风暴后倾斜了。
senses.why: A ship tips like a leaning column; this is a different, nautical word.
senses.whyCN: 船像倾斜的柱子；这是另一个航海用词。

senses.title: A cut edge of cloth
senses.definition: the selvage or list of cloth where threads finish
senses.definitionCN: 布料收边的织边
senses.example: The old coat shows its lists at the cuff.
senses.exampleCN: 旧大衣袖口露出布边。
senses.why: The border sense also lived in weaving.
senses.whyCN: 边界义也活在织造里。

senses.title: To set a price publicly
senses.definition: to state publicly the price of something for sale
senses.definitionCN: 公开标出售价
senses.example: The flat lists at two million.
senses.exampleCN: 这套公寓挂牌两百万。
senses.why: Goods entered on a price list take that price.
senses.whyCN: 进入价目表的货便取其价。

intro.en: The list of items comes from Old French liste 'border, edge strip', from Italian lista, likely from a Germanic word for a strip; the written row grew from a marked border. The ship\u0027s list is a separate Germanic word.
intro.cn: 条目之 list 来自古法语 liste「边条、镶边」，出自意大利语 lista，很可能源于日耳曼语「窄条」一词；书写的行列从「标出的边界」发展而来。船之倾斜是另一个日耳曼词。

items.en: A Germanic word for a strip or border is the likely origin of the border family.
items.cn: 日耳曼语「窄条、边界」一词很可能是边界词族的源头。

items.en: Italian lista meant a strip or border, and passed north with trade.
items.cn: 意大利语 lista 指窄条或镶边，随贸易北传。

items.en: Old French liste kept the border sense and added contest boundaries.
items.cn: 古法语 liste 保留边界义，并新增竞技场界线。

items.en: In Middle English the border became a written row of items.
items.cn: 中古英语里边界演变为书写的条目行列。

items.en: Modern English added official registers, prices, and kept the separate nautical list.
items.cn: 现代英语新增官方名录、标价，并保留独立的航海倾斜义。

note.en: Group one flags look-alikes; group two lists registers and rows.
note.cn: 第一组标出形近词；第二组列出名录与行列之词。

entries.definition: To pay attention with the ear; shares five letters, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 用耳倾听；共享五字母，词根不同。

entries.definition: An entry in a catalogue or an act of listing.
entries.definitionCN: 目录中的一项或列举动。

entries.definition: The beam above a door; no kinship.
A complete, organized list, often published.
entries.definitionCN: 完整有序的目录，常印行。

entries.definition: An official list of names or events.
A list of people on duty.
Things in a line, not necessarily written.
entries.definitionCN: 成行之物，不一定是写下的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the border trail and real phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用边界词路与真实短语。

normal.en: The written row began as a border strip, from Italian lista.
normal.cn: 书写行列源于边条，出自意大利语 lista。

normal.en: Knights once fought within the lists of the field.
normal.cn: 骑士曾于赛场界内比武。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: shopping list, wait list, blacklist.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：购物单、候补名单、黑名单。

normal.en: Ships list to one side in a storm — a separate word.
normal.cn: 风暴中船身倾斜——那是另一个词。

normal.en: Listless may come from the leaning list: lacking drive.
normal.cn: listless 可能出自倾斜义：缺了劲头。

abstract.en: Picture ten names stacked down one narrow page.
abstract.cn: 想象十行名字竖着排满窄窄一页。

abstract.en: Picture a knight stepping over a rope into the field.
abstract.cn: 想象骑士跨过界绳进入赛场。

abstract.en: Picture a ferry leaning as the waves push one side.
abstract.cn: 想象渡轮在水浪推压一侧时倾斜。

examples.en: Write your three choices on this list.
examples.cn: 把你的三个选项写在这张单子上。

examples.en: The hotel is fully booked, but we are on the wait list.
examples.cn: 酒店订满了，但我们在候补名单上。

examples.en: The boat listed badly until the cargo was shifted.
examples.cn: 货移走之前，船倾得很厉害。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「列斯特」——列得整齐最舒服 → 清单；列表

root: 条目义：古法语 liste「边条」（意大利语 lista，日耳曼来源）→ 书写的行列；倾斜义为独立的日耳曼航海词。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses gather at one edge: written rows, official registers, contest borders, woven edges, leaning hulls, and public prices.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项聚于同一条边：书写行列、官方名录、赛场边界、织边、倾斜的船体与公开标价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a marked strip that orders what lies along it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条标出的窄条，为沿其排列之物定序。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN ROW: items stacked one under another.
branches.cn: 书写行列：条目逐一下排。

branches.en: THE ROW WITH AUTHORITY: official registers.
branches.cn: 带权威的行列：官方名录。

branches.en: THE OLD BORDER: contest bounds and woven edges.
branches.cn: 旧边界：赛场界与织边。

branches.en: THE OTHER RAIL: a ship leaning to one side.
branches.cn: 另一条轨：船身侧倾。

branches.en: PRICES IN A ROW: goods take the listed price.
branches.cn: 成排的价格：货物取挂牌价。

intro.en: List is a borrowed noun with no prefixes; the family adds native suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: list 是无前缀的外来名词；词族靠本族后缀与复合构成。

latinIntro.en: No established Latin cognate exists, so the Latin section stays empty; the items show native word-building.
latinIntro.cn: 没有确证的拉丁同族词，拉丁部分留空；条目展示本族构词。

items.meaning: a border strip; a written row

definition_zh: 偷窃；窃取；剽窃
definition_en: to take something that belongs to someone else, without permission
core_image: 一只手伸进别人敞开的口袋
scene: 小偷从柜台后偷走了钱。 The thief stole the money from the counter.
sceneCN: 这里 steal 是「偷窃」（第 1 个义项）；句意：小偷从柜台后偷走了钱。

senses.title: Take without right
senses.definition: to take another person's property without permission
senses.definitionCN: 未经允许拿走他人的财物
senses.example: The thief stole the money from the counter.
senses.exampleCN: 小偷从柜台后偷走了钱。
senses.why: This is the plain physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最直接的物理义项。

senses.title: Take ideas
senses.definition: to use someone else's idea or work as if it were your own
senses.definitionCN: 把他人的想法或作品当作自己的使用
senses.example: He stole my idea for the design.
senses.exampleCN: 他剽窃了我的设计方案。
senses.why: An object can be taken, and so can a thought.
senses.whyCN: 物品能被拿走，想法也能。

senses.title: Move quietly
senses.definition: to move somewhere quietly so that no one notices
senses.definitionCN: 悄悄地移动到某处而不被察觉
senses.example: She stole into the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她悄悄溜进了房间。
senses.why: A thief moves in silence, so the silence itself became the verb.
senses.whyCN: 小偷行动无声，于是「无声」本身也成了动词。

intro.en: Steal goes back to Old English stelan, a strong verb of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: steal 可追溯到古英语 stelan，是日耳曼语来源的强变化动词。

items.en: The root meant to take secretly.
items.cn: 该词根意为秘密拿取。

items.en: Stelan meant to rob or take by stealth.
items.cn: stelan 意为抢夺或偷偷拿走。

items.en: Stelen kept the strong past form stole.
items.cn: stelen 保留了强变化过去式 stole。

items.en: Steal extended to ideas and quiet movement.
items.cn: steal 扩展到想法与悄悄移动。

items.en: The idiom steal the show named a scene stealer.
items.cn: 习语 steal the show 指抢尽风头的人。

note.en: Steal is compared with look-alike words and with words for taking wrongly.
note.cn: 把 steal 与形近词以及表示不正当拿取的词作比较。

entries.definition: a hard metal
hot water vapour
no longer fresh
to take from a person by force
to enter a building to steal
to reproduce someone's work

normalIntro.en: Steal starts with a hand in a pocket and ends with a silent step through a door.
normalIntro.cn: steal 从一只手伸进口袋开始，以无声的一步进门结束。

normal.en: Someone stole my bike.
normal.cn: 有人偷了我的自行车。

normal.en: Do not steal other people's work.
normal.cn: 不要剽窃别人的作品。

normal.en: He stole a glance at the letter.
normal.cn: 他偷偷瞥了一眼那封信。

normal.en: The cat stole into the kitchen.
normal.cn: 猫悄悄溜进了厨房。

normal.en: She stole the show with one song.
normal.cn: 她凭一首歌抢尽风头。

abstract.en: What is taken in secret still leaves a trace in the hand.
abstract.cn: 偷偷拿走的东西，仍会在手上留下痕迹。

abstract.en: A stolen idea never fits the thief.
abstract.cn: 偷来的想法，永远不合小偷的身。

abstract.en: Silence is the thief's loudest tool.
abstract.cn: 沉默是小偷最响的工具。

examples.en: The thief stole the money from the counter.
examples.cn: 小偷从柜台后偷走了钱。

examples.en: He stole my idea for the design.
examples.cn: 他剽窃了我的设计方案。

examples.en: She stole into the room.
examples.cn: 她悄悄溜进了房间。

dict_mnemonic.text: steal 是「偷」，过去式 stole、过去分词 stolen；东西能被偷，想法也能被偷，走路不出声也可以说 steal into。

root: 来自古英语 stelan（偷窃），源于日耳曼语；由秘密拿走财物，引申为盗用想法与悄悄移动。

sensesIntro.en: Steal means to take property, to take credit for an idea, or to move without a sound.
sensesIntro.cn: steal 指拿走财物、窃取想法，或无声地移动。

core.en: A hand closing on what is not its own.
core.cn: 一只手攥住不属于自己的东西。

branches.en: Coins leave a drawer in a closed fist.
branches.cn: 硬币在握紧的拳头里离开抽屉。

branches.en: A speech repeats another person's words.
branches.cn: 一篇演讲重复了别人的话。

branches.en: A door opens without a sound.
branches.cn: 一扇门无声地开了。

branches.en: Property and credit can both be carried off.
branches.cn: 财物与功劳，都能被带走。

branches.en: The quiet step is how the taking begins.
branches.cn: 安静的一步，是拿取的开始。

intro.en: Steal has irregular past forms and builds nouns of theft and secrecy.
intro.cn: steal 有规则外的过去式，并构成表示偷窃与秘密的名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

definition_zh: 不同的；有差异的；各自的
definition_en: not the same as another or each other
core_image: 一排颜色各异的杯子
scene: 美术课上，每人挑了一支画笔。 We all drew the same tree, but the pictures came out different.
sceneCN: 这里 different 是「不同的」（第 1 个义项：彼此不一样）；句意是大家画同一棵树，作品却各不相同。

derivatives.zh: 由 different 加名词后缀 -ence 构成，义为「差异」
由 different 加 -ly 构成，义为「不同地」
由拉丁词根 fer 派生的动词，义为「不同」

senses.title: Not the same as another
senses.definition: unlike something or someone else
senses.definitionCN: 与其他事物或人不一样
senses.example: This year's school trip is different from last year's.
senses.exampleCN: 今年的学校郊游和去年不一样。
senses.why: Two things carried apart leave a visible gap between them.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西被分开携带，之间便留下看得见的缝隙，这便是「不同」。

senses.title: Several separate ones
senses.definition: used before a plural noun to mean several unlike ones
senses.definitionCN: 修饰复数名词，表示若干个各不相同的事物
senses.example: We chose different books from the shelf.

intro.en: Courage comes straight from a Latin word for heart.
intro.cn: courage 直接来自一个表示「心」的拉丁词。

items.en: The Latin cor meant heart, the seat of feeling and will.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cor 意为心，被视为情感与意志的所在。

items.en: Coraticum, built on cor, meant matters of the heart, spirit.
items.cn: 建立在 cor 上的 coraticum 意为心事、精神状态。

items.en: Old French formed corage, meaning heart, inner spirit, boldness.
items.cn: 古法语形成 corage，意为心、内在精神、胆量。

items.en: English borrowed corage about the thirteenth century, first meaning the heart and its feelings.
items.cn: 英语约在十三世纪借入 corage，先指心及其情感。

items.en: Courage narrowed to mean bravery, the heart that holds firm.
items.cn: courage 词义收窄为「勇气」，即坚守的心。

note.en: These words share the heart root or name bravery.
note.cn: 这些词共享「心」的词根，或同样表示勇敢。

definition_zh: 当…的时候；虽然；然而；（一段时间）一会儿
definition_en: during the time that something happens, and also used to contrast two facts or to name a short period of time
core_image: 两条平行的钟表指针同时走着，一条走完另一条还在动
scene: 厨房里水在烧，她一边等一边切菜，两个动作同时进行。 She read the paper while the water was boiling.
sceneCN: 这里 while 是「当…的时候」（第 1 个义项：在某事进行的那段时间里）；句意为水开的时候她在看报纸。两条平行走的指针同时指着的画面就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: During the time that
senses.definition: used to say that one thing happens during the same period as another
senses.definitionCN: 表示一件事与另一件事发生在同一段时间内
senses.example: She read the paper while the water was boiling.
senses.exampleCN: 水开的时候她在看报纸。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply a stretch of time, and a clause placed inside that stretch gives the during meaning.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思只是一段时间，把从句放进这段时间里就产生了「当…时」的意思。

senses.title: Although
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to admit a fact that makes the main point surprising
senses.definitionCN: 用在从句开头，承认一个使主句令人意外的事实
senses.example: While the plan is cheap, it will take years to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划虽然便宜，却要花好几年才能完成。
senses.why: Two things placed side by side invite comparison, and when the second weakens the first the word leans to although.
senses.whyCN: 两件事并排摆放就会引来比较，当第二件削弱第一件时，这个词便偏向 although。

senses.title: Whereas
senses.definition: used to compare two facts and show that they are different
senses.definitionCN: 比较两个事实，显示二者不同
senses.example: Some people talk a lot, while others say nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人话很多，而另一些人什么都不说。
senses.why: The same side-by-side picture becomes a plain contrast when the two facts are simply weighed against each other.
senses.whyCN: 同样是并排的画面，当两个事实只是彼此对照时，就成了单纯的对比。

senses.title: A period of time
senses.definition: a short period of time, usually after the words a or for
senses.definitionCN: 一小段时间，通常跟在 a 或 for 之后
senses.example: Wait here for a while and I will be back.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里等一会儿，我就回来。
senses.why: This is the noun behind the conjunction: a while is the stretch of time that the clause later filled in.
senses.whyCN: 这是连词背后的名词：a while 就是后来被从句填进去的那段时间。

senses.title: To pass time pleasantly
senses.definition: in while away, to spend time in a relaxed way until it has passed
senses.definitionCN: 在 while away 中，指轻松地度过一段时间
senses.example: We whiled away the afternoon on the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在海滩上打发了整个下午。
senses.why: If a while is a block of time, then while away is the act of letting that block be used up.
senses.whyCN: 如果 a while 是一块时间，那么 while away 就是让那块时间被用掉的动作。

intro.en: While began as the Old English noun hwīl, a period of time, and only later became the conjunction that fills such a period.
intro.cn: while 起初是古英语名词 hwīl（一段时间），后来才成为填充这段时间的连词。

items.en: The stem hwī- meant a rest or a span of time in the older Germanic languages.
items.cn: 在较早的日耳曼语中，词干 hwī- 指一段休息或一段时间。

items.en: Hwīl was a noun, and the phrase þā hwīle þe, the time that, was its full form.
items.cn: hwīl 是名词，完整形式是 þā hwīle þe，意思是「…的那段时间」。

items.en: The long phrase shrank to while that and then to plain while, which took over the conjunction job.
items.cn: 长短语缩短为 while that，再缩成 while，连词职能便由它承担。

items.en: While spread into contrast and concession, replacing older words in ordinary prose.
items.cn: while 扩展到对比与让步，在普通文章中取代了更早的说法。

items.en: The noun survives in a while, once in a while and while away, keeping the original time sense.
items.cn: 名词义保存在 a while、once in a while 与 while away 中，保留了最初的时间意味。

note.en: The first group is the words one letter away in shape, the second the time and contrast words that do the same work.
note.cn: 第一组是字形只差一点的词，第二组是承担同样职能的时间与转折词。

normal.en: Side by side can mean at the same time, in contrast, or in spite of.
normal.cn: 并排既可以是同时，也可以是对比，还可以是让步。

normal.en: While away means letting the block of time run out pleasantly.
normal.cn: while away 是让那块时间愉快地流走。

normal.en: British writing adds a t and says whilst; ordinary speech does not.
normal.cn: 英式书面语加个 t 说 whilst，日常口语则不这样用。

normal.en: After a comma, while begins the second of two weighed facts.
normal.cn: 在逗号之后，while 引出两个被比较事实中的第二个。

abstract.en: See two clock hands turning at the same pace.
abstract.cn: 想两根同时同速转动的钟表指针。

abstract.en: Hear water boiling under a quiet page turning.
abstract.cn: 听水开的声响下面是翻书声。

abstract.en: Feel a stretch of time with nothing urgent in it.
abstract.cn: 感受一段没有急事的时光。

examples.en: He called while I was cooking dinner.
examples.cn: 我做晚饭的时候他打来了电话。

examples.en: While I agree with you, I cannot support this plan.
examples.cn: 虽然我同意你的看法，却无法支持这个计划。

examples.en: Let us rest for a while before we continue.
examples.cn: 我们歇一会儿再继续吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外欧」——望外一瞧，时间悄悄流过去一会儿。

root: 古英语名词 hwīl（一段时间）→ 中古英语 while；同族有 whilst、meanwhile、worthwhile。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a block of time, then fills that block with a clause, then weighs two clauses, and finally keeps the plain noun in a while and while away.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一块时间开始，用从句把这块时间填满，再让两个从句相互权衡，最后把朴素的名词义留在 a while 与 while away 里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two clock hands moving side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根并排走动的钟表指针。

branches.en: The simultaneity branch: boiling water and a newspaper.
branches.cn: 同时分支：烧水与看报。

branches.en: The concession branch: while the plan is cheap, it is slow.
branches.cn: 让步分支：计划虽便宜，却很慢。

branches.en: The contrast branch: some talk, while others say nothing.
branches.cn: 对比分支：有人话多，有人沉默。

branches.en: The noun branch: wait for a while.
branches.cn: 名词分支：等一会儿。

branches.en: The phrasal branch: whiling away an afternoon.
branches.cn: 短语分支：打发一个下午。

intro.en: While is a free Old English word; its family is made by compounds such as meanwhile and by the old -st form whilst.
intro.cn: while 是古英语的自由词；它的词族由 meanwhile 这类复合词和古老的 -st 形式 whilst 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin covered the same ground with dum and interim; the entries below are parallel forms, not the source of while.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 dum 与 interim 表达同样的意思；下面的条目是平行形式，并非 while 的来源。

items.example: It works as noun and conjunction.
items.exampleCN: 它既可作名词也可作连词。

items.example: It keeps the old noun alive.
items.exampleCN: 它让古老的名词义活下来。

items.example: It repeats the noun in idiom.
items.exampleCN: 它在习语中重复这个名词。

items.example: It turns time into a verb.
It is the bridge to the conjunction.

definition_zh: 个性；性格；人格；名人；魅力；地方或事物的鲜明风格
definition_en: the whole pattern of qualities that makes a person distinct, or a famous person, or the quality of being vividly oneself
core_image: 同一张素坯在窑里被反复上釉，最后开窑时只有它一只带着那种说不出名字的亮
scene: 面试官问了他三个问题，最后只记下一句：这个人说话时会停下来听别人说完。 The interviewer noted a personality that made the room slow down.
sceneCN: 这里 personality 指「一个人整体上给人的性格印象」（第 1 个义项：整体的性格格局）；句意是面试官注意到一种让整个房间放慢下来的性格。图中可辨识物件：面试桌、停在半空的笔、两份摊开的简历；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 名人（尤指娱乐界、媒体人物）

derivatives.zh: 使失去个性；使非人格化

senses.title: The whole pattern of a person
senses.titleCN: 一个人整体的性格格局
senses.definition: the total set of qualities that makes one person different from another
senses.definitionCN: 使一个人区别于另一个人的全部品质所构成的整体
senses.example: The interviewer noted a personality that made the room slow down.
senses.exampleCN: 面试官注意到一种让整个房间放慢下来的性格。
senses.why: the word was built from the name for a mask, so it names the face a person presents to the world in all its parts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「面具」一词构成，因此命名的是一个人向世界呈现的整张脸，连同它的各个部分。

senses.title: An object of psychological study
senses.definition: the measurable structure of traits that psychologists describe and classify
senses.definitionCN: 心理学家加以描述与分类的那些可测量的特质结构
senses.example: The field treats personality as a set of dimensions rather than a single score.
senses.exampleCN: 这个领域把人格当作一组维度，而不是一个单一分数。
senses.why: once qualities are counted and rated, the whole pattern becomes a research object with its own instruments.
senses.whyCN: 品质一旦被计数与评级，整个格局就成了一个有自己仪器配套的研究对象。

senses.title: A famous face
senses.definition: a well-known person, especially one who appears in media
senses.definitionCN: 广为人知的人，尤指常在媒体露面者
senses.example: A television personality opened the charity event.
senses.exampleCN: 一位电视名人主持了这场慈善活动。
senses.why: public life reduces a whole person to the face the public knows, so the word slides from the pattern to the person who carries it.
senses.whyCN: 公众生活把整个人压缩成公众认得的那张脸，于是词义从格局滑向承载它的那个人。

senses.title: Charm that fills a room
senses.titleCN: 能撑起一间屋子的魅力
senses.definition: a quality of presence that draws attention and holds it
senses.definitionCN: 一种让人注意并被吸住的存在感
senses.example: The old hostess had more personality than the whole cast.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老女主人比整台演员加起来更有魅力。
senses.why: when the pattern is vivid enough, it stops being a description and becomes an effect on others.
senses.whyCN: 当这个格局鲜明到一定程度，它就不再是描述，而成了对他人产生的效果。

senses.title: A place with a face of its own
senses.definition: the distinctive character of a building, street or brand
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、街道或品牌所带的鲜明性格
senses.example: The market kept its personality even after the renovation.
senses.exampleCN: 改造之后这个市场仍保有自己的性格。
senses.why: the metaphor is easy to move outward: whatever presents a consistent face to people can be said to have a personality.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻很容易向外搬：凡是向人呈现一致面孔的东西，都可以说有性格。

senses.title: A classified type
senses.definition: one of the recognised kinds into which patterns of character are sorted
senses.definitionCN: 把性格格局分门别类之后得到的某一类
senses.example: The test sorts people into four personality types.
senses.exampleCN: 这个测验把人分成四种人格类型。
senses.why: classification is the next step after measurement, and the noun then serves as the label of a class.
senses.whyCN: 测量之后的下一步是分类，这个名词于是充当某一类的标签。

senses.title: Friction between two patterns
senses.definition: the incompatibility that arises when two people's habits of behaviour do not fit
senses.definitionCN: 两个人的行为习惯合不来时产生的不相容
senses.example: The project failed on a personality clash, not on the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 项目败于性格冲突，而不是预算。
senses.why: the word can name a cause of trouble, which shows how much weight English gives to the pattern itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以命名麻烦的起因，可见英语把这个格局本身看得多重。

senses.title: Legal standing as a person
senses.definition: the status of being recognised as a person before the law, as held by a company
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上被认作人的地位，公司也可具有
senses.example: A company has legal personality separate from its owners.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在法律上具有独立于其所有者的人格。
senses.why: the oldest layer of the word is the mask that a role makes one wear, and law still speaks of the mask a body wears.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层是角色所戴的面具，法律至今仍在说某个实体所戴的那张面具。

intro.en: Personality comes from Latin personalitas, built on persona 'a mask, a character in a play'. The origin of persona itself is not established; the old explanation that it meant 'something through which sound passes' is a hypothesis. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: personality 来自拉丁 personalitas，由 persona「面具、剧中角色」构成。persona 本身的来源未得到证明；旧说认为它指「声音从中穿过之物」，那只是假说。年代均为约数。

items.en: Persona named a mask worn by an actor and, by extension, the role played. Its deeper origin is uncertain; a link to a borrowed Etruscan word is one hypothesis among several.
items.cn: persona 指演员戴的面具，引申为所演的角色。其更深来源不确定；认为它借自某种伊特鲁里亚词，只是若干假说之一。

items.en: The abstract noun named the quality of being a particular person, first in legal and theological writing about the status of an individual.
items.cn: 这个抽象名词指「作为某个特定个人的性质」，最早见于讨论个人地位的法律与神学文字。

items.en: English took the word in the eighteenth century for the sum of a person's qualities, at a time when portraits and novels were making individuality interesting.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪借入这个词，指一个人品质的总和，当时肖像画与小说正让「个体性」变得有趣。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century psychology turned it into a measurable structure, giving rise to tests, types and disorders.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪心理学把它变成可测量的结构，于是有了测验、类型与障碍。

items.en: Twentieth-century broadcasting made the word mean a famous face as well as an inner pattern, and the two senses now coexist.
items.cn: 20 世纪的广播电视让这个词既指有名的面孔，也指内在格局，两个义项如今并存。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of persona is a reconstruction, and the exact first English use of the abstract noun is not agreed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：persona 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式，这个抽象名词在英语中最早的确切用例也无公认结论。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the Latin word for a mask, whose meanings have drifted apart; group two holds the character words that overlap with this one.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「面具」一词、意义却已分流的词；第二组是与本词重叠的性格类词。

entries.definition: The plain noun for an individual human being; this word names the pattern that individual carries.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个的人的普通名词；本词命名的是那个人所带的格局。

entries.definition: Said of things that belong to or concern one individual, such as a personal letter; it never means 'full of character'.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于或涉及某一个人的东西，如私人信件；从不表示「有性格」。

entries.definition: Describes someone easy to like on first meeting, which is a social impression rather than a whole pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 形容初次见面就容易让人喜欢，是社会印象，而非整体格局。

entries.definition: The borrowed Latin word for the face one presents in public, often deliberately different from the private self.
entries.definitionCN: 借来的拉丁词，指在公众面前呈现的那张脸，常刻意与私下自我不同。

entries.definition: Overlaps in the sense of make-up, but character also judges moral fibre, which personality does not.
entries.definitionCN: 在「构成」这一义上重叠，但 character 还评判道德骨气，而 personality 不作此评判。

entries.definition: The part of the pattern thought to be native and steady; personality includes what experience adds.
entries.definitionCN: 格局中被认为天生而稳定的那部分；personality 还包括经验添上的部分。

entries.definition: The sense of who one is, including group membership; it answers 'who', while this word answers 'what kind'.
entries.definitionCN: 指「我是谁」的认知，包括群体归属；它回答「谁」，而本词回答「什么样」。

entries.definition: A technical term for the self as it mediates; it belongs to theory rather than to everyday description.
entries.definitionCN: 指起中介作用的自我，是理论术语，而非日常描述。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The base is Latin persona 'mask', so personality is the face a person wears in all its parts.
normal.cn: 词基是拉丁 persona「面具」，因此 personality 就是一个人戴着的那张完整的脸。

normal.en: The family runs person, personal, personality, personable, impersonate, depersonalize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 person、personal、personality、personable、impersonate、depersonalize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: personality traits, personality test, personality clash, television personality.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：人格特质、人格测验、性格冲突、电视名人。

normal.en: Psychologists speak of personality disorders, which shows the technical sense is a whole structure.
normal.cn: 心理学家谈人格障碍，可见专业义指的是整套结构。

normal.en: Law speaks of legal personality, keeping the oldest mask metaphor alive.
normal.cn: 法律说法律人格，让最古老的面具比喻继续活着。

abstract.en: Picture one plain bowl that takes glaze after glaze until only it shines that way.
abstract.cn: 想象一只素坯一遍遍上釉，最后只有它那样发亮。

abstract.en: Picture a room whose furniture rearranges itself around one guest.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子的家具围着一位客人重新排列。

abstract.en: Picture a signature that can be read from across the street.
abstract.cn: 想象一个隔一条街都能认出的签名。

examples.en: The job needs a strong personality and a thick skin.
examples.cn: 这份工作需要强势的性格和厚脸皮。

examples.en: Their personalities never meshed, though their skills did.
examples.cn: 他们的性格始终合不来，技能却互补。

examples.en: The magazine turned a shy researcher into a media personality.
examples.cn: 这家杂志把一位腼腆的研究者变成了媒体名人。

dict_mnemonic.text: person（人）+ ality（性质）——一个人整体的那种性质 → 个性、人格

root: 拉丁 personalitas，由 persona「面具、剧中角色」构成；persona 的更深来源不确定，借自伊特鲁里亚语之说仅为假说之一。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a mask is worn, and that mask is then read as a whole pattern, as something measured, as a famous face, as charm, as the face of a place, as a type, as a cause of friction and finally as legal standing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：一张面具被戴上，这张面具依次被读作整体格局、被测量的对象、有名的面孔、魅力、一个地方的脸、一种类型、摩擦的起因，最后是法律地位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one plain bowl that takes glaze after glaze until it alone shines in that particular way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只素坯一遍遍上釉，最后只有它那样发亮。

branches.en: THE PATTERN AND ITS INSTRUMENTS: first the whole make-up, then the same make-up turned into dimensions and scores.
branches.cn: 格局与它的仪器：先是整体构成，再是同一构成被变成维度与分数。

branches.en: THE FACE AND ITS FORCE: a famous face is the pattern reduced to what the public sees, and charm is that pattern acting on a room.
branches.cn: 面孔与它的力：名人的脸是被压缩成公众所见之物的格局，魅力则是这格局在一间屋子里起作用。

branches.en: THE SAME FACE ON THINGS: buildings, streets and brands are read as wearing a consistent face.
branches.cn: 同样的脸长在物上：建筑、街道与品牌被读作戴着一张一致的脸。

branches.en: FROM TYPE TO FRICTION: classification gives classes, and putting two classes in one room gives trouble.
branches.cn: 从类型到摩擦：分类给出类别，把两个类别放进同一间屋子就生出麻烦。

branches.en: THE MASK BEFORE THE LAW: legal standing keeps the oldest sense, where a mask makes a thing count as a person.
branches.cn: 法律面前的面具：法律地位保留了最古老的义项，面具使某物被算作人。

intro.en: The word is a Latin abstract noun built on the Latin word for a mask, so the whole family reads from that single image.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个拉丁抽象名词，建在拉丁「面具」一词上，因此整个词族都从那张面具读起。

latinIntro.en: Latin persona gives person, personal, personality, personable, persona and impersonate, all through the image of a mask and a role.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 persona 衍生 person、personal、personality、personable、persona、impersonate，全部经由面具与角色的意象。

items.example: The mask is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 那张面具是整个词族的根。

items.example: It produced the adjective of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 它造出表归属的形容词。

items.example: It turned the adjective into an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成抽象名词。

items.meaning: the quality of being a particular person

items.exampleCN: 面试官注意到一种性格。
那位候选人很讨人喜欢。
这些表格让申请人失去个人面目。

items.example: Every person wears a mask somewhere.
items.exampleCN: 每个人都在某处戴着面具。

definition_zh: 南方；南部；向南
definition_en: the direction opposite north, the southern part of an area, or toward the south
core_image: 指南针的红针指向下方，那里是温暖的南方
scene: 燕子冬天飞向南方。 The swallows fly south in winter.
sceneCN: 这里 south 是「南方」（第 1 个义项）；句意：燕子冬天飞向南方。

senses.title: The direction
senses.definition: the direction that is opposite north
senses.definitionCN: 与北方相反的方向
senses.example: The swallows fly south in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 燕子冬天飞向南方。
senses.why: This is the compass sense at the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最核心的方位含义。

senses.title: The southern region
senses.definition: the southern part of a country or area
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家或地区的南部
senses.example: He grew up in the south of the country.

senses.why: A direction becomes a place when people live there.
senses.whyCN: 当人们在那里生活，方向就变成了地方。

senses.title: Toward the south
senses.definition: in the direction of the south
senses.definitionCN: 朝南方的方向

senses.why: The same word serves as an adverb of direction.

intro.en: South is an old Germanic direction word tied to the sun.
intro.cn: south 是一个古老的日耳曼方向词，与太阳有关。

items.en: Suth meant the south.
items.cn: suth 意为南方。

items.en: The form became south.
items.cn: 词形变为 south。

items.en: It named both a direction and a region.
items.cn: 它既指方向，也指地区。

items.en: It also became an adverb, as in fly south.
items.cn: 它也成为副词，如 fly south。

items.en: Compounds like South Pole fixed its geography.
items.cn: South Pole 等复合词固定了它的地理用法。

note.en: South is compared with look-alike words and direction words.
note.cn: 把 south 与形近词以及表示方向的词作比较。

definition_zh: 心；心脏；内心；核心；勇气
definition_en: the organ that pumps blood; the center of feelings; the most important part
core_image: 胸腔里日夜跳动的不熄引擎：泵出生命也藏着感情
scene: 赛跑到终点，他把手按在胸口感受砰砰的跳动。 His heart was beating fast after the race.
sceneCN: 这里 heart 是「心脏」（第 1 个义项：泵血器官）；赛跑后胸口砰砰跳动，heart 正指这个身体器官。

senses.title: The organ that pumps blood
senses.definition: the organ in the chest that pumps blood around the body
senses.definitionCN: 胸腔中把血液泵送到全身的器官
senses.example: Exercise makes your heart stronger.
senses.exampleCN: 锻炼使你的心脏更强壮。
senses.why: The chest holds the body's pump, and the word names this vital muscle first.
senses.whyCN: 胸腔里装着身体的泵，这个词首先命名这块关键的肌肉。

senses.title: The center of feelings
senses.definition: the place where feelings are thought to live
senses.definitionCN: 被认为情感居住之处
senses.example: She thanked him with all her heart.
senses.exampleCN: 她全心全意地感谢他。
senses.why: Ancient people felt emotions in the chest, so heart became the home of love, courage, and sorrow.
senses.whyCN: 古人感到情绪在胸腔涌动，heart 于是成为爱与悲伤的居所。

senses.title: The most important part
senses.definition: the most central or important part of something
senses.definitionCN: 事物最中心或最重要的部分
senses.example: We walked to the heart of the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 我们走到了老城的中心。
senses.why: The heart sits at the center of the body, so any central place or idea can borrow the name.
senses.whyCN: 心脏位于身体中心，于是任何中心位置或要点都可借用此名。

senses.title: Courage or spirit
senses.definition: bravery and determination
senses.definitionCN: 勇敢与决心
senses.example: The team lost the match but never lost heart.
senses.exampleCN: 球队输了比赛，但从未失去斗志。
senses.why: Strong feelings power action, so heart also stands for the spirit that keeps you going.
senses.whyCN: 强烈的情感驱动行动，heart 也代表支撑你继续下去的精神。

intro.en: Heart is one of the oldest words in English, reaching back to the earliest Germanic.
intro.cn: heart 是英语最古老的词之一，可追溯到最早的日耳曼语。

items.en: Old English heorte meant the organ, the feelings, and the inner self at once.
items.cn: 古英语 heorte 同时表示器官、情感与内在自我。

items.en: It comes from the Germanic root *hertô, the standard word for heart in the family.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼词根 *hertô，是该语族表示心脏的标准词。

items.en: Latin cor and Greek kardia are distant Indo-European relatives of the same root.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cor 与希腊语 kardia 是同一词根的印欧远亲。

items.en: Old Norse hjarta reinforced the English form after Viking contact.
items.cn: 维京接触后，古诺斯语 hjarta 强化了英语词形。

items.en: Modern English added many idioms, such as learn by heart and heart of gold.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出 learn by heart、heart of gold 等大量习语。

note.en: Look-alikes and heart-family neighbours.
note.cn: heart 的形近词与词族近邻。

abstract.cn: 察觉情绪在胸腔涌起而非头脑：heart 是古人的情感中心。

abstract.en: See a map with a dot at the middle of the city.
abstract.cn: 看见地图上城市正中的那个点：heart 即中心。

examples.en: Doctors say a healthy heart needs regular exercise.
examples.cn: 医生说健康的心脏需要规律锻炼。

examples.cn: 他一个晚上就把整首诗背了下来。

examples.en: The small cafe is at the heart of campus life.
examples.cn: 这家小咖啡馆是校园生活的中心。

definition_en: to work for others, to provide food or goods, to hold a position, to spend time in prison, or to start play in tennis

scene: 这家餐厅供应新鲜的海鲜。 This restaurant serves fresh seafood.

senses.title: Work for others
senses.definition: to work for a person, group, or cause
senses.definitionCN: 为个人、群体或事业工作

senses.title: Provide food
senses.definition: to provide or put food on the table
senses.definitionCN: 提供食物或把食物端上桌
senses.example: This restaurant serves fresh seafood.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐厅供应新鲜的海鲜。
senses.why: Serving at table is a concrete kind of service.
senses.whyCN: 在餐桌旁服务是具体的服务。

senses.title: Hold a post
senses.definition: to hold an official position
senses.definitionCN: 担任官方职位
senses.example: He served as mayor for two terms.
senses.exampleCN: 他担任了两届市长。
senses.why: Public service is service in office.

senses.title: Spend time in prison
senses.definition: to spend a period in prison

definition_zh: 理解；懂得；了解；体谅；认为；听说
definition_en: to know what something means or how it works, or to know another’s feelings
core_image: 站在对方的立场上，忽然看清了他说那句话时的处境
scene: 老师把学生的作业本翻过来，看到他昨天晚上在页边写的一行小字，语气软了下来。 Now I understand why she left so early.
sceneCN: 这里 understand 是「理解、明白」（第 1 个义项：懂得含义或缘由）；句意为现在我明白她为什么这么早走了。站到对方位置上看清他的处境，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ing 构成名词，义为「理解；谅解」
动词加 -able 构成形容词，义为「可以理解的」

senses.title: To grasp the meaning of something
senses.definition: to know what words, rules, or ideas mean
senses.definitionCN: 知道文字、规则或想法的意思
senses.example: Do you understand the question?
senses.exampleCN: 你明白这个问题吗？
senses.why: The old verb stand means to be in place, so to understand is to stand in the place of a thing and see it from there.
senses.whyCN: 古语 stand 意为站立，understand 就是站到一件事的立场上去看它。

senses.title: To see the reason behind something
senses.definition: to know why something happened or was said
senses.definitionCN: 知道某事为何发生或被说出
senses.example: I understand now why he refused.
senses.exampleCN: 我现在明白他为什么拒绝了。
senses.why: Grasping a fact and grasping its reason are one act of standing in its place.
senses.whyCN: 抓住一个事实与抓住它的缘由，是同一个「站到它位置上」的动作。

senses.title: To know another person’s feelings
senses.definition: to be aware of and accept how someone feels
senses.definitionCN: 察觉并接受某人的感受
senses.example: My parents do not always understand me.
senses.exampleCN: 父母并不总能理解我。
senses.why: When you stand where another stands, feeling comes before facts.
senses.whyCN: 站到别人的位置上，感受先于事实到来。

senses.title: To believe or be told
senses.definition: to have been informed that something is so
senses.definitionCN: 据告知而认为某事如此
senses.example: I understand that the meeting has been moved.
senses.exampleCN: 我听说会议改期了。
senses.why: What you have taken in as true is also what you stand under as information.
senses.whyCN: 你当作真的收进来的消息，也是你站在其下接受的信息。

senses.title: To supply a missing word mentally
senses.definition: to take a word as implied though it is not written
senses.definitionCN: 把未写出的词含在心里补上
senses.example: In this phrase the verb is understood.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个短语里那个动词是隐含的。
senses.why: The reader joins the writer by standing in the same place and filling the gap.
senses.whyCN: 读者站到作者的同一位置，把空缺补上，两端就此接合。

intro.en: The word is an Old English compound of standing under something.
intro.cn: 这个词是古英语复合词，意为站在某物之下。

items.en: Understandan is built from under and standan, to stand, and means to stand in the midst of.
items.cn: understandan 由 under 与 standan（站立）构成，意为「站在其中」。

items.en: The prefix here is close in force to inter, so the word means to be among a thing.
items.cn: 这里的前缀效力接近 inter，因此这个词意为「处于某物之中」。

items.en: Middle English understand has already narrowed toward knowing and comprehending.
items.cn: 中古英语中 understand 已经收窄到「知晓、领会」。

items.en: The past forms understood, both past and participle, are leveled in the modern period.
items.cn: 过去式与过去分词在现代统一为 understood。

items.en: The polite sense of believing what one is told is common in business letters.
items.cn: 表示「据闻」的客气义在商务信函里很常见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs built on stand, and the near-meaning group collects verbs of grasping meaning.
note.cn: 形近组汇集由 stand 构成的动词，近义组汇集表示领会意义的动词。

entries.definition: the ability to grasp and to be kind
to grasp something wrongly
to stand against and resist
to grasp fully
to seize mentally
to share another’s feeling
to take the wrong meaning

normalIntro.en: Stand under a thing and look up at it from there, and you know how it stands.
normalIntro.cn: 站到一件事的下面抬头去看，就知道它到底是怎么立的。

normal.en: Understand and withstand share the verb stand, one standing among, one standing against.
normal.cn: understand 与 withstand 共用 stand，一个是站在其中，一个是顶住。

normal.en: Comprehend and grasp both picture taking hold, while understand pictures taking a place.
normal.cn: comprehend 与 grasp 都像伸手抓住，understand 则像占住一个位置。

normal.en: Understanding is the noun and also means a friendly tolerance between people.
normal.cn: understanding 既是名词「理解」，也指人与人之间的体谅。

normal.en: Misunderstand adds mis- for a wrong stand, a look from the wrong place.
normal.cn: misunderstand 加 mis-，表示站错了位置、从错处去看。

normal.en: Understood serves as both past tense and past participle.
normal.cn: understood 同时充当过去式与过去分词。

abstract.en: Step into another person’s shoes without saying a word.
abstract.cn: 不说一句话，把脚伸进别人的鞋里。

abstract.en: Look back at your own remark from there and feel it change.
abstract.cn: 从那儿回头看自己那句话，会觉得它变了样。

abstract.en: Then put a missing word into a gap and watch the sentence close.
abstract.cn: 再往空缺里填一个词，看句子合上。

examples.en: I did not understand the instructions at first.
examples.cn: 一开始我没看懂这些说明。

examples.en: She understands how hard the decision was for you.
examples.cn: 她明白这个决定对你有多难。

examples.en: We understand that the office will close early today.
examples.cn: 我们听说办公室今天会提前关门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的斯坦得」——安心地站在（stand）对方那边，自然就懂了。

root: 古英语 under（在其下／在其中）+ standan（站立），understandan 意为「站在其中」，过去式与过去分词均为 understood

sensesIntro.en: Each sense is a change of place: standing in a thing, in a reason, in a feeling, in a report, or in a gap.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都是一次换位：站进一件事、一个缘由、一种感受、一则传闻，或一处空缺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing where another stands and seeing what they see.
core.cn: 核心意象：站到别人站的地方，看见他所看见的。

branches.en: The language branch: meanings and implied words.
branches.cn: 语言分支：意义与隐含的词。

branches.en: The cause branch: why a thing happened.
branches.cn: 原因分支：事情为何发生。

branches.en: The people branch: standing inside another’s feeling.
branches.cn: 人分支：站进别人的感受里。

branches.en: The report branch: what one has taken in as true.
branches.cn: 传闻分支：被当作真而收进来的话。

branches.en: The plain classroom sense of getting the point.
branches.cn: 课堂里最普通的「听懂了」。

intro.en: Two native English pieces: a preposition of place and a verb of standing.
intro.cn: 两块土生英语部件：一个方位介词和一个站立的动词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 此词没有拉丁语来源，故拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Under here means in the midst of.
items.exampleCN: 这里的 under 意为「处于其中」。

definition_zh: 同班同学；同窗
definition_en: a member of the same class at school
core_image: 和你坐同一间教室的同桌伙伴
scene: 新学期第一天，教室里坐满了熟悉的面孔。 My classmates helped me carry the new books.
sceneCN: 这里 classmate 是「同班同学」（第 1 个义项：与你在同一班级学习的人）；句意是同学们帮我搬新书。

derivatives.zh: classmate 的基础词，义为「班级；课」
classmate 的构词成分，义为「伙伴；同伴」

senses.title: A student in the same class
senses.definition: a person who studies in the same class as you
senses.definitionCN: 与你在同一班级学习的人
senses.example: Wang Lin is my deskmate and classmate.
senses.exampleCN: 王林是我的同桌兼同班同学。
senses.why: Class plus mate simply names the fellow of your class.
senses.whyCN: class 加 mate，直接命名与你同班的人。

senses.title: A schoolmate of the same year
senses.definition: someone who was at school with you in the same years
senses.definitionCN: 与你同期在校学习过的人
senses.example: I met an old classmate at the bookshop.
senses.exampleCN: 我在书店遇到了一位老同学。
senses.why: Years later the same-year link keeps the name alive.
senses.whyCN: 多年以后，同窗之谊仍沿用这个名字。

intro.en: Classmate is a young compound: class plus mate.
intro.cn: classmate 是年轻的复合词：class 加 mate。

items.en: Latin classis meant a ranked division of people.
items.cn: 拉丁语 classis 指人的等级分组。

items.en: English formed class in the seventeenth century from classis.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语由 classis 构成 class。

items.en: Middle English had mette meaning a companion or equal.
items.cn: 中古英语 mette 义为「伙伴；同侪」。

items.en: Mate goes back to Germanic *gamatjon, one sharing food at a table.
items.cn: mate 可追溯到日耳曼语 *gamatjon，指同桌共餐者。

items.en: The compound classmate became common in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 复合词 classmate 在十九世纪普遍使用。

note.en: The first group gathers the -mate family; the second gathers school words.
note.cn: 第一组收 -mate 词族，第二组收校园类词。

entries.definition: A member of the same team.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「队友」，同用 mate 构词。

entries.definition: A person sharing a room.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「室友」，同用 mate 构词。

entries.definition: The room where classes meet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「教室」，词首与 classmate 相同。

entries.definition: A person from the same school.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「校友；同学」，范围更大。

entries.definition: The student sitting next to you.
A formal phrase for a student together with you.

normalIntro.en: Remember classmate as class plus mate.
normalIntro.cn: 把 classmate 记成 class 加 mate。

normal.en: mate means partner or friend.
normal.cn: mate 表示伙伴、朋友。

normal.en: teammate and roommate use the same pattern.
normal.cn: teammate 和 roommate 用同一构词法。

normal.en: a new classmate joins at the term start.
normal.cn: 新学期会有新同学加入。

normal.en: old classmates meet again years later.
normal.cn: 多年后老同学重逢。

normal.en: helping classmates makes friendship.
normal.cn: 帮助同学能增进友谊。

abstract.en: See two schoolbags side by side on one desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一张课桌上并排的两个书包。

abstract.en: Hear whispers about homework between two friends.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见两位好友间讨论作业的耳语。

abstract.en: Feel the joy of meeting an old friend after years.
abstract.cn: 感受多年后重逢老友的喜悦。

examples.en: My classmates and I cleaned the playground.
examples.cn: 我和同学们打扫了操场。

examples.en: A new classmate joined us this term.
examples.cn: 这学期来了一位新同学。

examples.en: She still writes to her classmates from primary school.
examples.cn: 她仍和小学同学通信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克拉斯美特」——克拉斯有个美好特好的同班伙伴。

root: class（拉丁语 classis，等级分组）+ mate（中古英语 mette，伙伴，出自日耳曼语 *gamatjon「同桌共餐者」）→ 现代英语 classmate；同类复合词有 teammate、roommate。

sensesIntro.en: Classmate names your present class fellows and, later, anyone who shared your school years.
sensesIntro.cn: classmate 既指现在的同班同学，也指同窗岁月里的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pupils sharing one classroom
core.cn: 核心意象：共用一间教室的两个学生

branches.en: A current class fellow
branches.cn: 现在的同班同学

branches.en: A same-year schoolmate
branches.cn: 同届同窗

branches.en: A partner in study
branches.cn: 学习上的伙伴

branches.en: A friend built at school
branches.cn: 在学校结下的朋友

branches.en: A face from past years
branches.cn: 往日岁月中的面孔

intro.en: The ending -mate builds a family of companions.
intro.cn: 后缀 -mate 构建了伙伴词族。

latinIntro.en: Mate is Germanic, not Latin, so no Latin entry sits here.
latinIntro.cn: mate 属日耳曼词源，此处无拉丁同族词。

items.example: Pass the ball to a teammate.

items.exampleCN: 她在市区遇到一位校友。

items.example: A book is a good companion.

definition_zh: 女王；王后；蜂王；纸牌皇后；（棋）后
definition_en: a female ruler of a country; the wife of a king; the single egg-laying female of a bee or ant colony; a playing card with a picture of a queen; the most powerful piece in chess
core_image: 一顶镶着细碎宝石的小冠，放在铺着深色绒布的桌上
scene: 王宫大厅里，侍从为一场加冕礼整理长袍和冠冕，门口的乐师反复校音。 The young queen stepped forward to greet her people.
sceneCN: 这里 queen 是「女王」（第 1 个义项：一个国家的女性统治者）；句意为年轻的女王走上前去迎接她的臣民。画面里可留意：长袍、冠冕、门口校音的乐师。

pos.zh: 女王；王后；蜂王；纸牌皇后；（国际象棋）后
使成为女王；（国际象棋）使兵升变为后

derivatives.zh: queen 加 -ly，指有女王气派的、威严而端庄的
queen 加 -ship，指女王的身份或王后之位
queen 与 size 复合，指加大号的床或家具

senses.title: A female ruler
senses.definition: a woman who rules a country in her own right
senses.definitionCN: 凭自身权利统治一个国家的女性
senses.example: The queen opened the new library herself.
senses.exampleCN: 女王亲自为新的图书馆揭幕。
senses.why: Old English cwen first meant woman or wife, and the sense of a ruling woman grew from the wife of a king who could hold power.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 cwen 本指女人或妻子，「执政女性」这一义项从可能掌权的国王之妻发展而来。

senses.title: The wife of a king
senses.definition: the wife of a ruling king
senses.definitionCN: 在位国王的妻子
senses.example: The king and queen greeted the guests together.
senses.exampleCN: 国王与王后一起迎接客人。
senses.why: The oldest use of the word for a royal woman was as the partner of a king, and that sense remains in titles.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指王室女性最古老的用法是作为国王的配偶，这层意思仍留在正式称谓里。

senses.title: The egg-laying female of a colony
senses.definition: the single female in a colony of bees or ants that lays all the eggs
senses.definitionCN: 蜂群或蚁群中唯一产卵的雌性个体
senses.example: The workers feed the queen and keep her in the warmest part of the nest.
senses.exampleCN: 工蜂喂养蜂王，并把她安置在巢中最暖和的地方。
senses.why: The one reproductive female of a colony holds a position like a ruler, so keepers gave her the royal name.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体中唯一负责繁殖的雌性地位如同统治者，养蜂人便给了她这个王室称呼。

senses.title: A playing card
senses.definition: the card in a set of playing cards that carries a picture of a queen
senses.definitionCN: 一副纸牌上印有王后画像的那张牌
senses.example: She won the trick with the queen of hearts.
senses.exampleCN: 她用红桃皇后赢下了这一墩。
senses.why: Card makers ranked the court cards, and the female figure beside the king took the word queen.
senses.whyCN: 纸牌制作者给宫廷牌排了等级，国王身旁的女性形象就用了 queen 这个词。

senses.title: The strongest chess piece
senses.definition: the chess piece that can move any number of squares in any straight line
senses.definitionCN: 能在任意直线上走任意格数的国际象棋棋子
senses.example: A pawn that reaches the far rank may become a queen.
senses.exampleCN: 走到对方底线的兵可以升变为后。
senses.why: The piece was once called the queen because it stood beside the king and moved with great freedom, and the name outlived its origin.
senses.whyCN: 这枚棋子当初因侍立在国王身旁、行走极为自由而被称为后，名字比它的由来活得更久。

intro.en: Queen is a native English word from Old English cwen, originally meaning woman or wife and related to words for woman in other old European languages.
intro.cn: queen 是英语本族词，来自古英语 cwen，本指女人或妻子，与欧洲其他古老语言中表示女人的词同源。

items.en: Cwen meant woman or wife, a neutral word for a female person.
items.cn: cwen 意为女人或妻子，是对女性中性的称呼。

items.en: The word is reconstructed in older Germanic as a term for woman, with relatives in other northern languages.
items.cn: 这个词在更早的日耳曼语中被重构为表示女人的词，在其他北方语言中有亲属词。

items.en: Middle English quen narrowed to the wife of a king and to a woman of royal rank.
items.cn: 中古英语 quen 收窄为国王之妻以及有王室身份的女性。

items.en: The spelling settled as queen, and the word spread to the female head of a colony and to cards and chess.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 queen，词义扩展到群体的雌性首领以及纸牌与国际象棋。

items.en: Modern English keeps the royal senses and the figurative senses of a leading woman or a dominant female animal.
items.cn: 现代英语保留王室义，也保留「杰出女性」与「群体中占主导的雌性动物」这类引申义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms that grew from the same word; the near-meaning group collects titles and words for female rulers.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一个词生长出来的形式；近义组收表示女性统治者与称号的词。

entries.definition: Having the dignity of a queen.
The position or rank of a queen.
Larger than standard, used of beds.
entries.definitionCN: 大于标准尺寸的，用于床。

entries.definition: An archaic word for a bold or disreputable woman.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧用法，指大胆或名声不好的女人。

entries.definition: A king, queen or emperor who rules a state.
entries.definitionCN: 统治一个国家的国王、女王或皇帝。

entries.definition: A woman who rules an empire.
The spouse of a reigning king or queen.
entries.definitionCN: 在位国王或女王的配偶。

entries.definition: A person who governs a country.

normalIntro.en: The word began as a plain term for a woman and rose to the throne; from the throne it spread to bees, cards and chess.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从对女人的平常称呼升上王座；又从王座扩散到蜜蜂、纸牌与国际象棋。

normal.en: Queen and quean look almost the same, but quean is an old insult while queen is a title.
normal.cn: queen 与 quean 拼写几乎一样，但 quean 是旧时的贬称，queen 是尊号。

normal.en: Queenly describes the manner of a queen, while queenship names her rank.
normal.cn: queenly 描述女王的气度，queenship 指她的身份。

normal.en: A queen bee is the only female in the hive that lays eggs, so the hive depends on her alone.
normal.cn: 蜂王是蜂巢中唯一产卵的雌蜂，整个蜂巢都靠她一个。

normal.en: The queen of hearts is a card, but the phrase also names a woman who wins hearts.
normal.cn: the queen of hearts 既是纸牌，也用来指赢得人心的女子。

normal.en: In chess the queen moves like a rook and a bishop combined, which makes her the strongest piece.
normal.cn: 国际象棋的皇后走法相当于车与象的合体，因此是最强的棋子。

abstract.en: A word for woman became a word for power, and the old plain meaning disappeared from ordinary speech.
abstract.cn: 一个指女人的词变成了指权力的词，而原先那个朴素含义从日常口语里消失了。

abstract.en: The queen in a hive rules by being the only source of the next generation, not by giving orders.
abstract.cn: 蜂巢里的蜂王靠成为下一代的唯一来源而「统治」，并不发号施令。

abstract.en: In chess the strongest piece is guarded most carefully, which says something about how power is kept.
abstract.cn: 棋盘上最强的棋子被保护得最小心，这本身就说明了权力是如何被守住的。

examples.en: The queen waved from the balcony as the crowd cheered.
examples.cn: 女王在阳台上挥手，人群欢呼。

examples.en: Only the queen of a hive lays eggs.
examples.cn: 蜂巢里只有蜂王产卵。

examples.en: He promoted the pawn to a queen and won the endgame.
examples.cn: 他把兵升变为后，赢下了残局。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「葵恩」——像向日葵一样被众人仰望的那位女性，就是 queen，女王。

root: 古英语 cwen（女人、妻子）→ 中古英语 quen（王后）→ 现代英语 queen；同族有 queenly、queenship、quean。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a woman of highest rank; the senses divide into a ruler, a royal wife, the female head of a colony, a card and a chess piece.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是地位最高的女性；义项分为统治者、王室配偶、群体雌性首领、纸牌与棋子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small jewelled crown resting on dark velvet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一顶镶着细碎宝石的小冠，放在深色绒布上。

branches.en: a hand raised to quiet a hall
branches.cn: 一只举起让大厅安静的手

branches.en: two thrones set side by side
branches.cn: 并排放着的两把王座

branches.en: a single bee at the centre of a comb
branches.cn: 蜂巢中央唯一的那只蜂

branches.en: a card turned face up on a table
branches.cn: 桌上翻开的一张牌

branches.en: a piece sweeping the whole board
branches.cn: 一枚横扫整个棋盘的棋子

intro.en: The word is native English, so its structure is mostly the old root plus English endings that name manner, rank and size.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，结构主要是古老词根加上表示气度、身份与尺寸的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 角色；作用；职责；地位
definition_en: the part an actor plays, or the function a person or thing has in a situation
core_image: 一卷写着台词的纸
scene: 她在剧中扮演一位年轻的医生。 She played the role of a young doctor in the play.
sceneCN: 这里 role 是「角色」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她在剧中扮演一位年轻的医生。

senses.title: Actor's part
senses.definition: the character that an actor plays in a film or play
senses.definitionCN: 演员在电影或戏剧中扮演的人物
senses.example: He won an award for his role in the film.
senses.exampleCN: 他因在这部电影中的角色获奖。
senses.why: The actor takes up one written part.
senses.whyCN: 演员承担起一份写好的台词。

senses.title: Function
senses.definition: the purpose or effect that someone or something has
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物所具有的用途或影响
senses.example: Salt plays a key role in the recipe.
senses.exampleCN: 盐在这道食谱中起关键作用。
senses.why: The part idea moves from stage to real life.
senses.whyCN: 「角色」这一概念从舞台走进现实。

senses.title: Duty
senses.definition: the expected duty or position of a person in a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在群体中被期待的职责或位置
senses.example: Her role is to train the new staff.
senses.exampleCN: 她的职责是培训新员工。
senses.why: A part in the group comes with duties.
senses.whyCN: 在群体中的位置伴随职责。

intro.en: Role comes from French rôle, a roll of paper with an actor's lines.
intro.cn: role 源自法语 rôle，指写着演员台词的纸卷。

items.en: Rotulus means a little roll of paper.
items.cn: rotulus 意为小纸卷。

items.en: Rotulus also gives the word roll.
items.cn: rotulus 也给出 roll 这个词。

items.en: Rôle is the roll holding an actor's lines.
items.cn: rôle 是写有演员台词的纸卷。

items.en: English role moves from the scroll to the part played.
items.cn: 英语 role 从纸卷转指所演的角色。

items.en: Role also means a function in a group.
items.cn: role 又指在群体中的作用。

note.en: A role is a part; a roll is a rolled object.
note.cn: role 是角色，roll 则是卷起的东西。
